[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Quantiles
[body] Quantiles are cutoff points that partition an ordered sample or dataset into equal-sized groups.
[body] • A median splits a sample into two: m • Two terciles split a sample into 3 groups: T1, T2 • Three quartiles split a sample into 4 groups: Q1, Q2, Q3 • Four quintiles split a sample into 5 groups: QU1, QU2, QU3, QU4 • . . . • Ninety-nine [per]centiles split a sample into 100 groups: P1, . . . , P99
[body] Prof. Oke (UMass Amherst) CEE 260/MIE 273 M1b: Summarizing Data September 10, 2026 11 / 16

[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Quantiles (cont.)
[body] Certain quantiles are equivalent to others:
[body] m = Q2 Q1 Q3
[body] • The median is the second quartile Q2 • The 25th percentile is equivalent to the first quartile Q1
[body] Questions
[body] 1 Quintiles (QU1, QU2, . . .) partition a distribution into 5 equal groups.How many quintiles are there?
[body] 2 The second quartile Q2 can be expressed as which percentile?a
[body] Answers: Q1: There are 4 quintiles; Q2: Q2 = P50 (fiftieth percentile)
[body] aRecall that a quartile splits a sample into 4 equal groups.
